svg.title: The toolbox checks the test really failed first, instead of taking anyone's word for it: The build check reads a repository that sits under /tmp, and still skips its tmp folders
svg.text: The toolbox checks the test really failed first, instead
of taking anyone's word for it
Scenario: The build check reads a repository that sits under /tmp, and still skips its tmp folders

g.text: Given a repository under /tmp adds a web service with no build task, and keeps a scratch
A copy of the toolbox's own repository, placed under /tmp the way a quick clone often is: pwd prints
/tmp/e2e-build-coverage. The developer adds a web service, project/web/docker-compose.yml, and writes no task to build
A scratch copy of that file sits in project/tmp. git status marks the new service "??", a file git does not track yet,
and the scratch copy "!!", a file git ignores: the repository's .gitignore holds the line tmp/.
Then the build check finds the web service, refuses it without its build
task, and leaves the scratch copy out
The build check is one of the checks task test runs first. It prints "6 Docker Compose
file(s) found": the five the toolbox already had, each with the task that builds it,
project:build:gitlab for instance, and the new web service.
The web service has none: "Missing task: project:build:web", and the check fails with the
exit code 201, the code Task gives a failed command. The scratch copy in project/tmp is not
The check reads each .gitignore line against paths inside the repository only. The line tmp/
leaves out project/tmp, and never the /tmp folder the repository sits in.
